subject: math
title: Binomial Theorem
syllabus: Binomial theorem for a positive integral index, general term and middle term, and simple applications.

body: (a + b)^{n} has n + 1 terms; the powers of a go down from n, the powers of b go up from 0.
T_{r+1} = C(n, r) a^{n−r} b^{r}
The coefficients are the n-th row of Pascal's triangle: each number is the sum of the two above it.
Middle term: T_{n/2 + 1} when n is even; two middle terms when n is odd.
Write the power of x in T_{r+1} as a formula in r, set it equal to the power you want, solve for r.
Term independent of x: set the power to 0. If r is not a whole number from 0 to n, there is no such term.
A product like (1 + 2x)(1 − x)^{n}: pick a term from the first bracket and the matching term from the binomial, then add.
Put x = 1: Σ C(n, r) = 2^{n}. Put x = −1: alternating sum = 0, so odd-place and even-place sums are 2^{n−1} each.
Σ rC(n, r) = n2^{n−1} · Σ C(n, r)^{2} = C(2n, n)
Differentiate (1 + x)^{n} to bring down r; integrate to get \f{1}{r + 1}.
Hockey stick: C(r, r) + C(r + 1, r) + … + C(n, r) = C(n + 1, r + 1).
\f{C(n, r)}{C(n, r − 1)} = \f{n − r + 1}{r}
Three neighbours in A.P. or in a given ratio → two equations in n and r.
Greatest coefficient of (1 + x)^{n}: the middle one(s). For (a + bx)^{n}, find where the ratio of neighbours drops below 1.
In (a^{1/p} + b^{1/q})^{n}, the term T_{r+1} is rational when p divides (n − r) and q divides r.
Count the r that work; irrational terms = (n + 1) − rational terms.
Sum of rational terms of (b + √{a})^{n} = \f{(b + √{a})^{n} + (b − √{a})^{n}}{2}.
Write the base as (multiple of m) ± 1 and expand: every term but the last is divisible by m.
Or find a power of the base that is ≡ 1 or −1 (mod m), then split the exponent.
Last two digits = remainder on division by 100.

traps: T_{r+1}, not T_{r}, carries C(n, r).
Keep the sign of b: (x − y)^{n} has (−1)^{r}.
r must be a whole number from 0 to n — otherwise the term does not exist.
"Coefficient" includes the numbers inside the brackets, not just C(n, r).
Odd n has two middle terms.
Remainder must be between 0 and m − 1: turn −1 into m − 1.

pyq.q: The coefficient of x^{48} in (1 + x) + 2(1 + x)^{2} + 3(1 + x)^{3} + … + 100(1 + x)^{100} is equal to
sol: Coefficient = Σ_{k} k·C(k, 48). Write k = (k + 1) − 1 and use Σ C(k, 48) = C(101, 49) (hockey stick).

pyq.q: Let C_{r} denote the coefficient of x^{r} in the binomial expansion of (1 + x)^{n}, n ∈ N, 0 ≤ r ≤ n. If P_{n} = C_{0} − C_{1} + \f{2^{2}}{3}C_{2} − \f{2^{3}}{4}C_{3} + … + \f{(−2)^{n}}{n + 1}C_{n}, then the value of Σ_{n=1}^{25} \f{1}{P_{2n}} equals.
sol: Σ C(n, r)\f{t^{r}}{r + 1} = \f{(1 + t)^{n+1} − 1}{(n + 1)t}; at t = −2 with n even this is \f{1}{n + 1}.

pyq.q: The sum of the coefficients of x^{499} and x^{500} in (1 + x)^{1000} + x(1 + x)^{999} + x^{2}(1 + x)^{998} + … + x^{1000} is :
sol: Coefficient of x^{k} = Σ_{j} C(1000 − j, k − j) = C(1001, k) (hockey stick).
